markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Existing margins describe training-pair separation. Their scale dependence prevents reliable comparisons across checkpoints. (2) Current probes never intervene on histories. They cannot distinguish recent-context reliance from broad historical association. (3) User feedback identifies redundancy and compatibility concerns. Histories alone do not establish ownership or fulfilled demand, so these remain hypotheses.

**Related work.** (1) HSTU provides the required sequential backbone [1]. Its architecture does not establish that a particular checkpoint uses order effectively. (2) Recency research motivates measuring sensitivity to recent interactions [2]. Temporal contrastive work cautions that perturbations can disrupt semantics [3]. (3) Sampling-reliability research separates sampled discrimination from broader recommendation quality [4]. Diagnostic ranks must therefore retain the benchmark’s candidate protocol and remain supplementary.

These insights suggest three directions: sequence-sensitivity auditing, rank-based separation diagnostics, and evidence-qualified relevance auditing.

### Framework

| Direction | Observable evidence | Unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Separation | Target rank and negative-outranking fraction | Generalization beyond sampled candidates |
| Sequence sensitivity | Paired rank changes under controlled interventions | Whether sensitivity reflects useful intent |
| Relevance evidence | Explicit title/description specifications | Unobserved compatibility and purchase intent |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Matched history-intervention audit — 6/8/3.** Originality: controlled comparisons unify familiar probes, but introduce no new estimator. Potential: actionable HSTU diagnosis, but perturbations can be unrealistic. Difficulty: reuses inference hooks, but requires careful padding and paired aggregation [1–3].
2. **Rank-based separation dashboard — 3/6/2.** Originality: useful replacement for scale-sensitive margins, but standard rank statistics. Potential: interpretable comparisons, but candidate dependence remains. Difficulty: simple scoring, but eligibility and ties require care [4].
3. **Specification-evidence audit — 6/7/6.** Originality: separates relation, compatibility, and information sufficiency, but follows existing task definitions. Potential: explains actionable mismatches, but incomplete descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: small audit is feasible, but credible labels need human review [5].

### Selected idea: matched history-intervention audit

At 0% progress, prioritize an inexpensive diagnostic before changing training. Freeze each category’s single HSTU model. For identical users, targets, and candidates, compare original histories with equal-count recent removal, oldest removal, and repeated shuffles preserving the final item.

Strip padding before intervention and restore left padding afterward. Extract features at the final nonpadding index, never `count−1`. Report paired target-rank changes, reciprocal-rank changes, and HR@10 flips with eligible-user counts; bootstrap users within categories while retaining each user’s perturbations together.

Recent-removal damage relative to oldest-removal damage suggests recency reliance; final-item-preserving shuffle damage suggests earlier-order sensitivity. Neither proves intent understanding or predicts improvement. Preserve the fixed host macro HR@10 for selection; do not train additional predictors or combine scores.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [3](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-8994/17/10/1634), [4](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086), [5](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html).

idea.description: Extend the family-aware HSTU diagnostic adapter with matched history interventions that measure recent-context and earlier-order sensitivity using one frozen trained model per category.
idea.motivation: The existing adapter measures embedding geometry and sampled training margins but cannot test the diagnosis that recommendations rely on broad historical associations. Controlled paired interventions provide measurable sensitivity evidence without inventing intent, compatibility, or ownership labels.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Preserve existing ModelView interfaces and use view.model.eval() under torch.no_grad(), restoring its previous mode afterward. Loader batches support training-context sensitivity only; label those results accordingly. Run validation sensitivity only when the host explicitly supplies permitted validation contexts and fixed candidates through an existing interface. Exclude padding and reserved tokens from candidates; reuse identical candidates across interventions. For left-padded sequences, locate the greatest index containing a nonzero item. Exclude histories shorter than three interactions from matched deletion comparisons, remove k=min(3, floor((n-1)/2)) items, and report excluded counts. Repeat final-item-preserving shuffles with a local seed-42 generator. Return null with a reason for undefined metrics. Preserve all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], seed settings, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. No architecture or inference change is required; retain checkpoint and embedded predictor consistency. Supplemental diagnostics must not replace the host evaluator or select perturbations using held-out test data.

originality.positive: Combines matched recency deletion and final-item-preserving order interventions within the HSTU compatibility adapter.
originality.negative: The interventions and paired rank statistics are established diagnostic techniques rather than a new learning algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Provides a practical basis for choosing subsequent single-model HSTU changes and testing whether they alter sequence reliance.
future_potential.negative: Sensitivity alone cannot establish recommendation usefulness, causal intent, or improved validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the trained model, sequence feature hook, and candidate scoring interface without additional training.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding, eligibility, tie handling, repeated perturbations, and user-level aggregation require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU as a sequential-transduction architecture for recommendation.
limitations: Architecture-level results do not establish recent-context or order reliance for the supplied checkpoint.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Motivates examining excessive dependence on recent interactions.
limitations: Does not establish whether this benchmark's HSTU models exhibit harmful recency bias.

related_work.title: Temporal-Aware and Intent Contrastive Learning
contributions: Motivates caution when cropping, masking, or reordering sequential histories.
limitations: Perturbation-based findings require controls and do not directly identify user intent.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies
contributions: Distinguishes sampled discrimination from agreement with fuller evaluation and other reliability dimensions.
limitations: Does not validate any proposed diagnostic as a predictor of HSTU performance on this task.

related_work.title: TREC Product Recommendation Task Definitions
contributions: Distinguishes substitutes, complements, compatibility, and subjective preference.
limitations: Relation labels alone cannot establish redundancy, fulfilled demand, or compatibility when specifications are missing.
